text_fidelity_a:
Push-Up Pump [[VIDEOID:mo2U0MH5NGR4RTX]]This is a great little push up device. It's easy enough so that anyone can do a push-up or two with it, even your grandma. But, it also gives your upper body a really good workout even if you can do a lot of push-ups.

I really like how this device encourages great posture and discourages hyper-extension of joints. Push-ups would be a nearly perfect exercise if people didn't hyper extend their joints or over strain their weak parts when doing them. This device fixes everything by using your body weight to give you exercises that you can actually do.

This has helped me a ton with my upper body strength. It works, and I definitely recommend it.

Now, for the negatives.

The tension bands are a joke. Unless you either cut them apart or use all 65 lbs of them, they'll make a horrible snapping noise. You'll end up just throwing these away.

This won't last forever. It's not the sturdiest construction, and the design puts some weird strains on some of the joints, so it's only a matter of time before this falls apart. But you should get about a year of good use out of it, and by that time you'll be doing push-ups on your own.

The legs/feet of this should have been about twice as long, to make this sturdier. As it is, the only balanced position is with the seat placed on my upper stomach. If they were longer, then I could pick where I wanted to place my body on this.

And dismounting takes a lot of practice, and the fabric part peals off the first day you use it.

But overall, I'd heartily recommend it, especially if you've always dreamed of being able to do a lot of push-ups. No matter what your fitness level, this will definitely push you to the next level with push-ups.

Pros:
+Great way to work up to doing push-ups
+Great way to rapidly increase the number of push-ups you can do
+Fits away easily in a corner
+It's sturdy enough for what you need it for

Cons:
-You won't ever use the tension bands
-It's not the sturdiest construction. Expect it to break after about a year of use.
-Comes with fabric that's warping and pulling off
-The legs should have had more surface contact with the floor, to make this more steady
-I fell off this quite a few times when trying to stop doing push-ups, so it will take some time to get used to dismounting this device
text_fidelity_b: Push-Up Pump

text_fidelity_a:
Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire I purchased Campy Shamal 2-way rims a couple years back. I then purchased everything needed to mount and maintain tubeless tires including Fusion 3s. I ride a '12 Specialized S-Works Roubaix and mostly do fast training rides about 3 to 4 days a week with longer rides beyond 60 miles fairly regularly. I weigh out at roughly 185 pounds.

Tubeless and ceramic bearings are somewhat in the same category these days in terms of bikers wondering if this equipment truly makes a difference. Well, I've ridden ceramic bearings in my crank and in my wheels...and YES...it makes a difference...now...I've ridden on tubeless for two riding seasons...and YES...they make a difference. Tubeless is the future...as it is in nearly every vehicle that has wheels from a riding mower to a motorcycle to a car...and mountain bikes. Why it has taken so long with road biking is understandable...change is hard...and manufacturers will go where the money is.

First, let me make this clear...putting the Fusion 3 tires on was a chore...and I mean...a CHORE. It will test your patience. Do NOT succumb to using levers as it will ruin the bead. Google tubeless tire installation for help but even then it will baffle you as to how you're going to get that tire over the rim...but...you will...and the benefits will be worth it.

Second, it takes a few rides to get the tires truly seated. Use an air compressed pump if you've got it...but...I had a "Joe Blow" floor pump that worked fine. I didn't install the sealant until after the second short ride and pump up. You will most likely lose quite a bit of air at first but as the tire seals over time...the air pressure stabilized. I do pump up my tires before every ride but it isn't out of the norm of my former clincher tires.

Third, I've ridden my fusion 3s at 90psi on the front tire and 100psi on the back. The ride is fast & super smooth. A lot of riders think super high psi is better but that is, (arguably for some), not true because at a high psi your tire is actually bumping up and down off the road which drains energy transfer over time. The benefit of running tubeless at lower psi is that the tire remains in more constant contact with the road which...over time...equals better energy transfer...and hence...speed, comfort, and endurance. Also, there is some evidence that without a tube you eliminate friction...I'm honestly not sure about that claim...even so, I can say from experience that I'm not going back to tubed tires...tubeless tires run as advertised.

Fourth, durability...I run typical roads here in Maryland over countless miles...up and down hills...less maintained side roads...and these Fusion 3s can go yet another season. The wear is normal with no unusual issues. I've NOT had one flat tire. I've NOT added more sealant since the first install...which I should've done...but...it hasn't made a difference.

Fifth, the only reservation I have is getting a flat tire but I guess it's a good thing that I'm not as use to dealing with flats like I had for my tubed tires. I have to say it has been a pleasure to not have had one flat for two seasons.

I'd like to try the ATOM version of this tire...and I think I'll get it just for comparison purposes. Not looking forward to the install and my expectation is that they will not fit my riding style, endurance expectations, and my higher weight...even so, I'm a believer in trying anything once...so...we'll see.

All in all...educate yourself but don't be afraid to go tubeless. It is change that we all seem to avoid but I'll never go back now that I've tried it out...and as the biking money goes...tubeless quality and selection will as well. ENJOY!
text_fidelity_b: Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire

I think the main - perhaps only - thing we noticed in difference is that mine is slightly heavier. Otherwise, for these beginners, they are each excellent and very similar. Perhaps as we get better we will find other differences, but as beginners, we each love the paddle we have and to us, they are almost one and the same. Again, note that mine is blue and slightly heavier, while hers, this JOOLA Vision Pickleball Paddle with Textured Carbon Grip, is slightly lighter and black. But beyond that, they seem to us to be similar in build. Our hits are going to continue to improve along with our confidence. I have to say, I do notice the weight more, but I have no issue - and this ever-so-slight weight difference is one that does not affect my swing. However, my wife does say she prefers her lighter version.

The area we both love about the JOOLA is the grip. Without question, of all the paddles we have, the JOOLA's grip is the best, top of the heap, and the reason we'd (so far) pick a JOOLA over the others. As we get better, that may change. But for both of us, we feel far more connection to the paddle than we have with others. So in the end, grip alone sells us on this JOOLA Vision Pickleball Paddle with Textured Carbon Grip.
text_fidelity_b: JOOLA Vision Pickleball Paddle with Textured Carbon Grip Surface Technology for Maximum Spin and Control with Added Power - Polypropylene Honeycomb Core Pickleball Racket Available in 14mm and 16mm

text_fidelity_a: Hit-Air Airbag Vest Light Weight (LV) I've had  a 11 year old quarter horse/connemarra mix gelding for almost three years. His history was unknown when I bought him.  He's a beautiful horse, but has needed complete re-training. He can be spooky on trails when we go out alone - which is something I do a lot (3-5 times a week) as there aren't many people to ride with where I'm located. So, I wear the vest every time I go out and carry my cell phone to be safer.  I've come off 3-4 times in the last three years when he has spooked while trotting because he tends to spin around -- and this vest has allowed me to get up with NO injuries, no soreness and NO fear.  Before I bought the vest, I would be very tense during our rides, but now I'm relaxed knowing that if he does have a bad spook while trotting through a field, I'll be ok. AND as he has gotten more used to trail riding alone, it is happening less and less. Highly recommend this vest. My only issue is deflating it when I re-mount after is has deployed. I'm sure there's. a way to do It, but I haven't taken the time to figure it out.....yet.
text_fidelity_b: Hit-Air Airbag Vest Light Weight (LV)

Upon closer inspection with a magnifier, I see that a hunk of the bearing surface was gone, like it had cracked off and disappeared. I am the only user, and I know I didn't drop anything... so I can't figure out what happened here, except to suspect a manufacturing defect? Dunno.

Will call RCBS tomorrow and find out if I can get a replacement.

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of quality extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can securely stash a few things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is wide, strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

Made by Coleman, like I said, and with lots of nice features, this high quality cooler is a must-have and a great gift. Check out the same cooler with other team logos. Just make sure you get the one like this one from "TLG8," to get the high quality one I just described. Thanks for reading my review. Hope it helped someone.
text_fidelity_b: NCAA Kentucky Wildcats Can Cooler, 16

text_fidelity_a:
Tasline Elite Pure Spectra Solid 8X Strand Braided High Power Premium Fishing Line Picture shown is 40lb on a Tranx 401HG

I have been buying from Australia and dealing with the shipping cost and time to get here, so very happy to see it here in Amazon.

This is an excellent braid. Over the years I have spent thousands and thousands of dollars on fishing braid trying to find that "one". If I don't like a braid after one or two sessions, I will pull it all off my reel and throw it in the garbage. I don't like lines that have dyes that bleed off. I also don't like lines that depend on coatings on them as they can have a waxy feel to them, which I feel affects the casting. Some coated lines also take time to break in, and some coatings eventually just wear off. This is one of the many things that makes Tasline so different. They don't use any dyes or coatings. So there is nothing to break in, wear off, or bleed.

Due to the diameter to breaking strain ratio of this braid, and I am able to get more line on my reel. I recently just spooled up 1000m of 20lb braid on my Tern 400. Tasline 20lb has a PE rating of 1.7 and breaks at 34lb which is absolutely perfect for slow pitch jigging setups.

Casting is phenomenal. I think that the 8 strand braids in general are just smoother than the more common 4 strand braids. This line is very quiet going through the guides, and knot retention is excellent.

*Each spool has a hand written number on the back which correlates with breaking strain testing data for that specific spool. My testing has shown that these numbers are accurate and true.
text_fidelity_b: Tasline Elite Pure Spectra Solid 8X Strand Braided High Power Premium Fishing Line

After having it for over a year now I believe, it still works perfectly and I haven't had any issues with it. If you're looking for something cheap that'll get your back, back into shape this is the best way to do it at an affordable cost.

I would definitely recommend this product to my friend as well.

text_fidelity_a:
Unknown Camco 51089 9" Aluminum Ultralight Tent Stake, (Pack of 6) I was looking for a strong, lightweight alternative to the heavy-duty, 12-inch tent stakes that came with my big expedition tent. The bag of stakes weighed over 10 pounds, and I really wanted to lighten it up to keep the tent package under the airline's 50-pound maximum. There are a few plastic stake alternatives that I know from experience just don't last long before they break. And there are many 7-inch stakes of this design that are just too short. Finally, I found these 12-inch aluminum stakes. I used them on a recent moose hunt in western Alaska and found them to be adequate, for the conditions we encountered.

On the positive side, these were long enough to reach through the tundra lichens and reach the rocky soil below. I used a small (8-ounce) hammer to pound them in, and they held through moderate winds that we had one day. (The rest of our 9-day trip was gorgeous weather with only light breezes). They weigh about 1/4 of what the heavy-duty steel stakes weighed, which allowed me to add a ground sheet and floor liner to my tent bag, and keep the whole package at or below the original tent weight.

These don't have the surface area and therefore the holding power of the bigger, heavy duty stakes, and they will probably bend if you strike them too hard into rocks or tree roots. None bent on my recent trip, but I've used the smaller, 7-inch versions of these on other tents and have bent plenty of them, so I was being gentle. I expect that they'd do really well in good, firm soil, but they probably lack the surface area to hold well in sand or snow, and probably won't stand up to rocks and solid tree roots very well. I have, and recommend carrying, a variety of tent stake styles. I like to include a few bigger/beefier stakes to use for the high-stress areas of the fly and door, on the windward side of your tent. These 12-inch stakes would be good for those spots on smaller tents. I use the bigger aluminum military-style blade stakes, or the twisted MSR cyclone stakes (of stronger aluminum) for the critical areas on my bigger tents that require better anchors. I also like to have one or two of the original steel stakes for tougher, rocky spots where I need a good anchor.

Overall, these Camco 12-inch stakes are a good addition to my tent bag, but not a perfect solution by themselves. Maybe one day soon someone will make aluminum stakes this length with the width, surface area, and strength to truly replace those heavy but effective steel stakes.
text_fidelity_b: Unknown Camco 51089 9" Aluminum Ultralight Tent Stake, (Pack of 6)

text_fidelity_a:
Concept2 RowErg Indoor Rowing Machine - PM5 Monitor, Device Holder, Adjustable Air Resistance, Easy Storage I have owned most types of exercise equipment out there: treadmills, climbers, Spinbikes, recumbent bikes, total gym, ab machines, ellipticals, weight benches and all sorts of small do-hickys that were made to help you maintain or get into shape. No, I'm not a shopaholic LOL I am naturally small to average size but need to stay fit and healthy. Over the past year or so I have hit that dreaded time my mom and Aunts always warned about: that time when everything you ate stayed with you and loosing a quick five pounds was no longer a simple thing. One big note here though; One of the reasons I have had so many different types of exercise equipment over the years is, I have cerebral palsy and need to stay at a healthy weight and try to keep flexibility and cardiovascular health as high as I can have. Unfortunately I have found that many types of exercise equipment have something that prohibits me being able to use them effectively. For example, the total gym is a great piece of equipment however most of the exercises that I want to use involve laying on your back with your knees bent and your feet flat on the slide board. For me it is nearly impossible because of my muscle tightness I am unable to do that as well as a lot of the other exercises that require a bit of balance or flexibility that I just don't have. I also have weaker leg muscles so a lot of the other equipment seemed to either wear me out immediately, or I'd have to used my upper body exclusively. Several months ago I began thinking about a rower. I actually ordered and canceled a different, less expensive rower that had gotten good reviews here because I'd been reading independent review sites and the Concept 2 had always gotten great reviews and I knew I wouldn't be happy with lower quality. The water rowers looked good too but frankly I couldn't swing the cost especially since as much as I hoped a rower would work for me I knew the odds were I'd be selling it if it wasn't something I could use well.
Assembly was probably the easiest of anything I've ever owned. The hardest part was getting the two pieces out from the Styrofoam! LOL Eight screws and the screwdriver was included. The item is well-made and feels sturdy but wasn't too heavy for me to assemble on my own very easily. All you are doing is attaching a V shape bracket to the rower and then down to the flat piece that sits on the floor. Once assembled you just lift the front piece of the machine (one handed it's not too heavy) and the back part has a little hook shaped end that goes down on a bar on the front piece and you lower the machine and the parts lock together. The machine is long but narrow. Storing may not be as easy as a machine that just folds but stays in one piece, but on the other hand having the two pieces come completely apart could make storage easy if you needed to put each piece away in different area.
Now for the usage: As I have said I do have limitations and I do know they make a different model that sits up higher off the ground and it is supposed to be easier to get on and off if you have any type of balance or mobility issues however I chose this model because I felt it would be easier for me to get on and off. I did have to make one adaptation: because I do not have normal flexibility, I found that once my feet were strapped in I could not quite reach the handlebar to begin rowing, so I borrowed my Service Dogs tug rope she uses to open doors and attached it to the handlebar of the rower. It gives me the extra length that I need that once I am seated with my feet strapped in I can use the rope and pull the handle bar up to begin rowing. If you are heavier or built where you're not able to reach the bar comfortably this is an easy fix.
When I first began using the rower I found as I had expected that I was using very little to no legs, however after just a week I am able to use my legs some. Nowhere near the "normal" amount of a correct row form where your legs are doing about 60% of the work, but I have seen enough improvement already to know that as I continue my leg strength will improve enough to where I will be rowing in a more full body natural form. The reason I am saying this is just to let you know that even if you are limited and you're not able to start out with the "correct" rowing style, you can still use this machine. I think it is important however to know what the correct form is. I would suggest going to the Concept2 website and watching a video. It's not difficult at all but I do like to remind myself as a row that it's legs core arms and then arms core legs. Since I did not have leg strength to begin with I needed to be aware of not pulling with my back. They also have a great video on adaptive rowing for those with physical limitations. So you can see that this really is something that everyone can use and benefit from.
The machine is quite. Not silent but you can watch TV while using it without having the volume to max. You set the amount of air to allow through the machine by sliding a "damper" lever. The more air the more resistance but your pull also makes a difference so you can get a more challenging workout just by changing when and how fast you pull. The monitor is small but the numbers are large and easy to read. It has several features but I find the "Just Row" is what I'm using now. I also have an app on my phone and the rower and my phone connect via Bluetooth and it will log my information so I can have a record of my workouts. The app also offers a verbal feature so if you are visually impaired you can know how you are rowing as far as distance and time.
They also have software that allows you to see yourself in a boat rowing against other people that you can see on a monitor or your tv.
Even though I've only had the machine two weeks I can easily say it will be one of the very few that I will keep and use. It is by far my favorite and I'm already seeing improvements. I have lost 5 pounds and know that I am improving not only my cardiovascular system but I am getting stronger and more flexible as I can see improvements in my leg use. I started with 0% legs and now am maybe 10% and that's a big improvement that will only get better. Oh and I will add that it is FUN!!! I actually enjoy rowing. Something about the repetitive movements and sound I find enjoyable.
I do not give five stars often at all because I am extremely critical and consider all factors. This rower and the company has not only met but exceeded my expectations and I would recommend it without hesitation.
I'm looking forward to using this for years and seeing a real improvement in my health and happiness. If you have been considering this rower I would say go for it!
text_fidelity_b: Concept2 RowErg Indoor Rowing Machine - PM5 Monitor, Device Holder, Adjustable Air Resistance, Easy Storage

text_fidelity_a:
Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle I've had this bike a few months now. It is quiet (but not silent, there is a noise from the drive belt) but it is very smooth and responsive.

Assembly was straight-forward, but unless you want to find all the tools you need to assemble it yourself, I would recommend getting the tool package available on their website. The torque wrench was our deciding factor in just buying their kit. Keiser offers a discount on the tool package if you purchase it with the bike directly on their website.

Things to know: the app is TERRIBLE. Other reviewers have already listed all the bugs in depth, but the app is unreliable for recording workouts and is not user-friendly. The bike also will not work directly with other apps (like Peloton). For that you need the converter, which costs another $200 on top of this bike, unless you buy the bike directly from their website. Then it is only $50. Considering they were discounting it 75% with purchase of the bike, I consider $200 a rip-off for what your bike should have done in the first place (work with other apps). I wrote customer service about the bugs. They agreed there was a problem and the developer would be notified. I was told I would be updated when it was fixed. I never was. The problem in the app still persists as of my writing this review.

Customer service: I wrote customer service via email. As far as timeliness, they wrote back quickly. However, if I ever had more than one question in my message, one, and only one, of my questions would be answered. I had to write back multiple times for my additional questions to be answered, so one simple email took several days to be fully addressed. As stated above, some of the issues never were.

text_fidelity_a:
Nautilus R616 Recumbent Bike (Discontinued) This bike comes in a large box that makes it obvious what’s inside of it. If you have people that might steal your packages around, you might want to make arrangements to be there when this arrives. It’s on the heavy side, also, so the mail person might appreciate some help, too! ;)

You’ll have to assemble it, so make sure you set aside a good hour/hour and a half to put it together. It’s pretty simple and straightforward, though.

This bike has Bluetooth connectivity, but we never could get proper connection. Thankfully, the bike works perfectly fine without it. My husband has a Bluetooth device, but I don’t. That means we can both use it, with or without Bluetooth(should it ever connect properly).

One feature I like is that the seat slides back and forth with ease. While sitting on the seat, just pull down a little bar beside the seat, and slide it into the perfect position. Then, just push the bar back up to lock the seat in place. This makes the bike work for lots of various positions and leg lengths.

The main part of the bike comes fully assembled. (It’s the seat and top and all that needs assembly.) At one point, I was pedaling along and I started hearing a rattling noise. I became worried, thinking the bike was already messed up. Thankfully, it was only one of the circle pieces around the pedal that had popped off. I had to turn it a bit to lock it back into place. This part and most of the base is plastic, so I’m a bit concerned about the lasting quality of it.

The power cord is detachable. To me, that gives it a bit of a cheaper feel, but at the same time, it does make it easier with little ones around. When not in use, I can roll up the cord and tuck it out of sight, and no one is tripping around cords. But, once again, I’m a little concerned about the lasting quality of such a “light” power cord.

Overall, though, it’s a pretty nice bike. It’s comfortable to use, and for a piece of exercise equipment, it really doesn’t take up a ton of space.
text_fidelity_b: Nautilus R616 Recumbent Bike (Discontinued)

Seems to work Ok so far (more below). The camera didn't come with a memory card - so I purchased a 32GB Samsung EVO memory card to use in it - wanting to see if that would be adequate - and it was. I also bought a large package of the Energizer MAX alkaline batteries. The manual recommends using rechargeable batteries and I will probably do that later - as this camera can run down batteries fairly quickly.

I did have some issues with the camera - number one, there was a problem with the strap/buckle that lets you strap the camera to a tree or post. Nothing major - the stitching came loose. I was still able to make it work though and will probably replace the strap when I go to use this camera in the field. The second issues was with getting the motion-sensor function working. It would trigger once and then not again. I played around with the settings and seemed to get it to work - but have no idea what actually fixed the issue.

The camera takes great photos - I've mainly been using it in the time-lapse mode (since I was having issues with the motion function). The photos are very clear and sharp. Daytime photos more so than night, but that's to be expected.

All-in-all I'm happy with the camera and look forward to using it this summer and the coming fall.

Camp Chef Pro 30 Single Burner Stove Pictures don't really show the sturdy construction or impressive size of the Pro 30. I'm currently using it without the leg extensions, but they are just as solid as the rest of the unit. With a 14x16 inch cooking area, it can handle quite a load.

I do a LOT of outside cooking, including roasting my own coffee. I had been using a 12,000 BTU side burner on an old, rusted out gas grill to roast green coffee beans, but the side burner recently died and I had no interest in refurbishing the gas grill. I needed a new stove for roasting coffee beans. After considering all the options, I chose the Camp Chef Pro 30. I'm glad I did.

Roasting coffee beans on the side burner limited me to calm, no wind days for the quickest roast. Roasting a pound of coffee usually took 19-21 minutes; longer in any wind. The wind was howling with gusts to 25 MPH for my first coffee roast with the Pro 30, a true test of the stove. After adjusting the air intake behind the low-med-high knob, I had a flame that held up nicely to the wind. With the Pro 30, in the strong wind, I roasted a pound of green coffee in 12 minutes on the medium setting!

I've been roasting coffee for about two years, on average one roast every 7 days. The wind will no longer be a factor and the Pro 30 will save me a lot of time. I own the Camp Chef Rainier table top stove for camping, and can serve 2-4 people easily with it, but could not use it for roasting coffee with the 10" Dutch oven I use. With the Pro 30 and a big pot of chili, stew, or soup, I'll be able to serve a large family. For the $70 I paid for the Pro 30 here on Amazon, it is a GREAT value!
text_fidelity_b: Camp Chef Pro 30 Single Burner Stove

text_fidelity_a:
Ultralight Portable Outdoor Backpacking Canister Camp Stove with Piezo Ignition 3.9oz (Silvery Stove and Orange Box) Great little stove, love the piezo lighter. Fits inside a hiking pot with a fuel canister, very easy to keep with you and very fast to set up. Perfect for a hot cup of coffee or some soup while out in the woods or while taking a break from work. For the cost of a couple foofy coffee drinks from Starbucks, you can have fresh coffee wherever. This much utility for this cost can't be beat.

For those unfamiliar with micro canister stoves, there are some limitations. This is definitely is a backpacking stove, and nothing like a Coleman suitcase or even one of the older green single burner Colemans. This stove is optimized for light weight and compromises have been made in support of that goal. The pot supports are small and somewhat wobbly and the base is your canister, so smaller canisters are less stable. Definitely not meant for large pots, even a full 1liter pot is pretty wobbly. I've had trouble making enough coffee for 3 people with each of us wanting to fill our 20+ oz insulated travel mugs, even though the stove cranks out plenty enough BTUs. Wound up stacking up bricks around the stove to support the pot independent of the stove, so all the stove had to do was pump out BTU's. This is not a detraction, just something to be aware of, as heating 2+ liters of water for a group is NOT what this stove is designed for.

I use this for a quick cup of coffee or some hot soup while camping/shooting/wrenching/whatever. Morale booster, mostly. I've had no issues with reliability, but if I was in any kind of situation where the stove failing would be more than an inconvenience, I'd cough up for the peace of mind of an MSR. Sure it's 4-5 times the cost, but that's only $30.

Note: There are adapters all over the web to use these with the very inexpensive tall skinny butane cans, or even to refill the isobutane canisters with just butane. For the average hiker using a stove a few times per year, not enough fuel will be used for fuel cost to matter. If you're using it more frequently, one of those adapters could pay for itself quickly. Straight butane won't work as well as isobutane in cooler weather, but if you're getting into temps that low you should probably look at a liquid fueled stove anyway.

Wow that got long.
text_fidelity_b: Ultralight Portable Outdoor Backpacking Canister Camp Stove with Piezo Ignition 3.9oz (Silvery Stove and Orange Box)

I usually use only one or two bands, depending on the exercise, because the full 120 lbs of resistance with all 3 bands is usually too much for my workouts.

It's also light enough and compact enough that I can throw it in my suitcase when I travel. It's also way better than all the equipment in most hotel gyms. At first, I was going to throw away the closed door attachment, and I'm super glad that I didn't. It's awesome! text_fidelity_a: Coghlans Waterproof Matches 10 Pack These are very good waterproof matches - as good as any other set I've ever used.  Bear in mind, however, they aren't magical.  It's still difficult to keep anything alight in a driving rain or heavy winds.  And, yes, they will not light if the striking surface is ruined, if struck under water, or in the vacuum of space.  For waterproof matches, they are very good.  As a fire starter, matches - in general - are adequate.  These should be kept in a nicer sealed matchbox with a protected striking surface (Coghlans makes a nice one that also includes a whistle and signal mirror), and you should have AT LEAST one other backup fire source that might mitigate the shortfalls of matches, if designated for a situation where fire starting is critical.  I never have less than three, when I go off-trail - usually waterproof matches, a [[ASIN:B0013L8D9K Swedish Firesteel]], usually a lighter or two, and sometimes a fire piston along with some good emergency tinder.  I wouldn't feel right with just one of any of these firestarters.
text_fidelity_b: Coghlans Waterproof Matches 10 Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Intex Challenger Kayak, Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars and High Output Air-Pump This thing is amazing!! I've taken it out 6 times over the last month, for 2–5 mile jaunts, at local city lakes and sheltered bays, and a couple lakes in a National Park. At this point it's already worth its price: if it failed next outing (I don't think it will) I'd still be happy with it. For less than 100 bucks I have the ability to visit little islands inside lakes, get unbelievable views from the water, and explore wetlands and sloughs that landlubbers can't get to. I can't get over the novelty of launching, docking at some isolated rock beach or island to eat a snack, then coming back over the water. And having the ability to do this where there are no concessionaires almost feels like cheating! The experience is just that amazing. Not to mention ease of transport and storage.

As far as seaworthiness: yes, it tracks poorly even with the skeg but that just means more rotational practice for you. Stable in lake waves and jetski wakes, I've never felt close to capsizing. It's slow. Will blow with the wind if you let it, but you can easily paddle against it. It works, and it'll get you there.

Setup and teardown is easy but it does take some time. The pump is fine and it will inflate faster than you think. For durability: all components feels very heavy and solid, it's like bounce house material. The valves feel strong and actually take some effort to release the air. I take care not to beach the kayak, or set up/tear down on any surface too rocky or spiky. I also take lengths to dry it afterwards: I point fans at it for a few hours, making sure to get the inside crevices dry. I feel optimistic it'll be fine for a while.

Standard hacks: Get a large IKEA blue bag to carry the actual deflated kayak, use the included (flimsy) bag for the other components, pump, your PFD. Don't inflate the seat-bottom for more vertical leg room.

When researching this, I talked to 2 paddling-adventure friends and inflatable kayaks are perfectly respectable and even the choice of some extreme adventurers: see Audrey Sutherland's amazing books and adventures, and look up Grabner inflatables. Enjoy!!!
text_fidelity_b: Intex Challenger Kayak, Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars and High Output Air-Pump

text_fidelity_a:
Bayou Fitness Total Trainer 4000-XL Home Gym I've been using the total trainer for about 9 months now and I'm finally comfortable leaving my thoughts on it. Overall, I think this is the best value in a Total Gym type of machine and I would not hesitate to recommend it to others. I love mine.

---------------------------------------
Pros:
Huge glide board

Large range of resistance settings

Ability to add free weights

Comes with a curl bar (though I found it less than useful for actual curls) and other attachments that you may find useful.

Great price to performance ratio

Cons:
Some limitations for strength once you get into better shape, but with true, proper form which makes the exercises much harder and humbles guys who think they can really bench 260lbs because they hold the weight and move their arms 10 inches up and down 5 times in a row, this machine will last most average or out of shape people for quite a while.

The video that comes with it is pretty lame in my opinion, you're better off searching youtube for demonstrations of exercises on a Total Gym and doing those.
---------------------------------------

The machine can support up to 385lbs, so if you're 180lbs and add 100lbs of weights, you're still way under the limit. The maximum resistance levels are 69% without the glide board pulley engaged and 38% with. So technically, at 180lbs, the maximum resistance you're going to get is 106lbs and 193lbs. That sounds like a lot, but keep in mind that most of the common exercises seem to work better with the pulley engaged (and some would be impossible without it since the cable/rope is a fixed length and way too long to use without the pulley to take up the slack). For example, the instructions show you a way to kneel on the board, attach the mini-pulleys to the glide board and do a bicep curl with the curl bar. This is pretty unstable at resistance level 11 (the board wants to slide out from underneath you and you're really pulling yourself high into the air (I hit my head on my basement ceiling trying the exercise this way). While trying to keep the board from moving around underneath you is a decent way to work your core, it detracts from the exercise. I've found that bicep curls work best with the pulley engaged and the user hanging upside down, curling the fly handles up towards the chest (search [Total Gym upside down bicep curls] on youtube for an example). Still, for most people who are not in great shape, curling 106lbs isn't easy with good form (arms straight down at the sides on every rep reset, curl all the way up to the chest keeping the wrists straight and the elbows at the sides near the hip as much as possible). You could also invest in a weight vest to wear and increase the overall weight. Bayou Fitness could solve this issue by providing another, shorter cable that would allow certain exercises like the upside down bicep curl, chest fly, upright row and so on to be done without the middle glide board pulley being used.

Also, I'm not sure I'd bother with the squats on this machine, they don't allow you to have proper form because the glide board restricts movement (search [proper squat form] on youtube or Google to see what I mean). For some people the movement on this machine might not be a bad thing, but in my case, it causes pain in the knees whereas normal, proper form squats do not.

For those than cannot do a pull-up to save their lives, this machine can help with the large muscles involved (shoulders, biceps, triceps, upper back), but only actual pull-ups will work the stabilizer muscles. Still, if you're upper body is pretty weak or out of shape, this will get you more than 4/5 of the way there with the extra 100lbs (again, provided you use proper form and pull your elbows down towards your hips and keep your shoulders up and back and your head up during the exercise). Eventually, you'll need to start doing actual pull-ups to work the stabilizers and your core to get real results.

The instructions show a method of doing a bench press using the side pulley attachment points and thereby NOT using the middle pulley, which gives you a max resistance level of 69% of your body weight + 100lbs of plates on the bar attachment (this should be able to allow anyone up to about 230lbs to at least bench their own weight). However, the method they describe actually promotes improper form (but a slight adjustment will allow good form provided you aren't too wide). on a bench press, you want the bar to come down towards your nipple area, not your neck or collar bone (doesn't work the chest well and can produce injuries). Your elbows should be bent down towards your hips or sides. If you're willing you slide your body up on the board so that the side pulleys line up with your nipple area (which leaves your head hang off the board a bit and makes the cables come up underneath your armpit area but allows the proper motion for a bench press) you can get a decent bench. Two things with this. 1, don't wear loose shirts when doing this, they will get caught up in the pulley and 2, always keep the footboard attached for this exercise in case you cannot finish a rep, simply put your foot straight down to catch your body and there's no way for the bar to trap you or crush your chest. In essence, this allows you to bench as much as the machine will take without a spotter and without the same risk of injury that comes with lifting free weights on a bar (if you have good form otherwise you'll get injured even if you don't fail the lift). I do wish that the bar was wider for those of us with longer arms (closer grip stresses the triceps instead of the chest). There may be some ways around that last limitation, but I haven't found one that ensures that the cables will not slide on the bar that is also completely safe. zin theory, you could get a regular free weight bar and two 2.5lb slotted plates to thread the cable heads through so they don't move, but then you're adding 5lbs of weight plus a 25-45lb bar, which makes the exercise a bit more dangerous.

The few suggestions I'd make to Bayou Fitness would be a shorter cable to allow certain exercises to be done without the pulley, a wider curl bar to help isolate the chest when using that for benching and the ability to add more than 100lbs to the glide board weight bar. I'm not sure if the last one is possible (I'm assuming that the limitation is based on the strength of the bar and not the glide board), but the other two should be no problem. But overall, for most people looking to get into better shape, this machine and adherence to proper will get you there provided you put the time into it.
text_fidelity_b: Bayou Fitness Total Trainer 4000-XL Home Gym

text_fidelity_a:

Max Weight [[VIDEOID:22f19394a4eb7cc9583d0dd8639034c0]] Finally coming back to review this bike, purely because of the fantastic support I received. I bought this bike to bridge a 2 month gap where I was going to be without my road bike, but we (wife and I) ended up using it up until now (~16 months). Usage is ~30 mins a day per person, almost every day, with...medium intensity? My wife and I are both ~140lbs for what it's worth.

Downsides are:
1) no electronics (cadence, resistance level indicator, etc)
2) The saddle wasn't great for us, but we swapped our own saddle in anyway
Upsides are:
1) Price
2) no electronics to break - yes, i listed that as a downside as well : )
3) dirt simple setup

After setting up, it did take a bit of tightening and tweaking here and there to get out all the kinks in terms of squeaks and whatnot, but this is to be expected with any bike IMO. Also worth noting that we both ride with noise cancelling headphones.

Product support story:
After a year and half of daily riding, we finally noticed a little bit of a clunk in the crank, that would happen as soon as weight shifted onto each pedal. Now, I had already gotten my money's worth out of this bike, but on a whim I decided to investigate a bit. I eventually discovered that the main weld on the axle was starting to crack (see photo/video). Figured it was worth a shot to see what product support would say, even though this isn't covered under warranty. What happened next blew my mind - support got back to me within one day, covered the part for me for FREE, and shipped it out immediately using FEDEX! I swapped the part in and all is well again.

I would absolutely buy this bike again, or any other Sunny bike.

These are amazing pumps, combining 2 stages with pressure sensing and auto shutoff.
My Tuomico 20PSI failed the first day of use on the beach in Sullivan's Island SC. In my experience, the first stage blower motor is the most fragile part, and may either last for many uses or fail on the first or second use. This was a hot day at the beach, and my larger size SUP, and the pump started screeching and changing speed noticeably and then died. The SUP was nearly inflated (almost ready for the 2nd stage) and I was quite disappointing. After a few minutes the 2nd stage pump started by itself and finished the inflation to target pressure. However, after the unit fully cooled the first stage never worked again and I returned the pump for a refund. I think the motor burned up. I keep looking for a higher quality pump, and with a large SUP, I may pre-pump a couple minutes to reduce blower time & over-heating. The first stage draws about 8-9 amps, and the 2nd stage only 4-5 amps.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 4 Special Edition Fitness and Activity Tracker with Built-in GPS, Heart Rate, Sleep & Swim Tracking, Black/Granite Reflective, One Size (S &L Bands Included) The fitbit as it comes out of the box (in late 2020) has lots of bugs. The settings function will lock it up if you try to use it. The weather app errors. It will not sync reliably. You would be thinking about returning it right now. But if you do some internet searches, you will find that these are known bugs that it leaves the factory with. If you install the mobile app, sync it and wait about 2 - 3 days the nyou will get the update that makes things work as they should. Do NOT uninstall the weather function of the fitbit just because it won't sync. If you do, it will no longer be available to re-install when device is updated. Just leave it there and wait for the update. Then weather and settings will work and syncing will become reliable.

It's absurd that fitbit would release such a defective product, but they do and they don't make any effort to tell you about the needed update.

After updating, it is quite a handy little tracker. The only fitbit tracker with a built in gps so you don't need to take your phone along. However be warned that your battery if fully charges will only last 4 - 5 hours when using the gps. It also takes a lot of time away from the standby time remaining.

Another feature they don't try to explain properly is the Spotify integration. Your fitbit can act as a very basic remote control for Spotify, but only if you subscribe to Spotify Premium. This means that to use the Spotify remote control feature you need 1) a paid Spotify subscription and 2) you need to have your phone with you. No music can be downloaded to the fitbit. It is just a simple play/stop/skip remote function for your phone and Spotify paid.

So those are all the things that fitbit doesn't want to tell you even after you buy it. After you get it updated, it is essentially a Charge 3 with built in battery sucking gps and paid Spotify remote control.

If you are new to fitbit and don't mind all the hassles getting it working right, it is a great little tracker. If you are thinking about upgrading from a fitbit Charge 3, the built in gps and Spotify remotes are the main differences.

Update: After all this it would never sync reliably. I would always have to reboot the device twice in a row to get sync started again. This hat do be done about every 36 hours.

Returned. Not worth it.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 4 Special Edition Fitness and Activity Tracker with Built-in GPS, Heart Rate, Sleep & Swim Tracking, Black/Granite Reflective, One Size (S &L Bands Included)

NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates for Women Men Double Row Shiny Indoor Outdoor Skates for Unisex Girls with Shoes Bag [[VIDEOID:6a9dae27c4383bb5bbbf63af76ea0b65]] A year ago my wife was using roller blades, but wanting a pair of roller skates to also enjoy. A year ago, she severely broke her foot and was sidelined for seven months, but limited as she came back. Now she’s able to do more, cleared for roller blading, but she had been wanting those skates... so when I had the chance to grab her this pair, I took it. She had to wait awhile, but now she’s had a chance to get on them... These NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates are decent, what she described as good for beginners and moderate skaters, but she had a few things to mention. First, she has a foot size that can be spot on 9 or 9.5 with a range that could workout between, based on the show and it's cut. In this case, ordering online, she wasn’t able to try them on first. In the end, she feels like the overall fit around the foot is good, but snug. The front of the boot - at the toes - is the tightest. She first tried with thicker socks, but settled for compression socks, which worked much better. Leather can sometimes adjust to a foot, stretching a bit to hug a foot, but in this case, we’re not sure. She says the front at the toes is tough - the leather hard - so she can’t imagine it stretching. In the end, she feels like if you’re spot on a size, you should be okay, but if there is even a slight “off” about a foot size, there could be an issue.

Second, The skates look nice, and overall the materials. - leather - seems good. The materials in the base and wheels seem good. They have wheels that are supposed to light up as they role - they do, but it’s hard to see in the light/daylight. We have not tried them in the dark, and we do see a little sparkle, but overall, you’re not going to be rolling in the dark, so what we are seeing, it’s not overly impressive. There is a little video above, but yea, the “light up” to us is not impressive. Third, She loved roller skating as a child through to young adult and wants to go back to doing it again. She loves loves loves roller blading, but there is something about skating she holds dear... We will say, her being unable to do anything like this in a year has made it hard for her - she felt it hard/big/painful and has to take this slowly getting back to it. She got up, she went, and she really liked it a lot. She felt like it’s coming back and she enjoyed the experience. She feels like these NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates are going to let her get back up and going - with time to develop - and she’s going to be able to enjoy it. But she also feels like these are beginner to moderate level. The ground itself - the surface - is important. The place we took them (parking lot) was rough and uncomfortable for her. She does have an area she loves for blading, but during several months a year (current) we have a massive amount of acorns that fall and she cannot, for safety, blade (or roller skate) in the area. So this parking lot showed her not every surface is going to work with these skates.

Overall, these ARE decent skates. Things to consider: size, type of sock, surface for skating. These will have an affect on the experience. She sets them best for beginner to moderate. And in the end, she does like them and thinks she’ll get a good amount of use out of them.

Fitbit Inspire HR Heart Rate and Fitness Tracker With S and L Bands, White, One Size, 1 Count Brand new out of the box, trying to set it up, and this thing is already presenting challenges. If you're thinking of getting one here's what you need to know: the charger is magnet so it attracts the charging prongs to the device easily HOWEVER, the magnet isn't strong enough to hold onto the device. If you set it down, it pops off the charging cord. You have to lay it down, propped on something, veeeerrrrrry carefully. I haven't even worn this thing and I can see that this is going to drive me nuts!!! I may deploy some high tech hacks - like a twist tie or some masking tape - to content with the charger design. :-p I'll come back and write more once I've set up and worn this thing.

You should know, I"m a devoted fitbit user and wear my devices out - they retire off to wherever beloved exhausted devices go after their life ends. I'm so sad my Alta HR died. I want it back! I still have my old Flex as a backup. I've never considered buying another brand of tracker and probably never will.

2/8/2020 - I'm back and I've upgraded stars from 3 to 5. The magnetic charger thing is still a bummer but absolutely everything else about this tracker is phenomenal. I can't believe this thing has so many features at its price point. Interaction with the screen is intuitive. The features available on-screen are a step up from the Alta HR. There's a Breath/relax/meditation function, a Timer, you can view and enable/disable the silent alarm settings right on the device, you can see how many steps you have left to meet the Reminder To Move target. I simply ADORE this thing!!! Fitbit, you really brought it with this tracker. I thank you.

7/7/2020 Back again with more information. Exactly 6 months after purchase, the device won't sync so I tried pairing it again to Bluetooth. The device won't pair so I tried resetting it per Fitbit product help web pages. The device won't reset. Now what? I loved the features on this device but it's hard to love something that won't work. Back to 3 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Inspire HR Heart Rate and Fitness Tracker With S and L Bands, White, One Size, 1 Count
